title: Roy Palmer and what became of the Chicago band members
summary: Roy Palmer and Amos Riley; Pops Foster's Christmas cards; Johnny Lindsey and Herbert Lindsay; whether they are alive.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: Chicago girl now. See? See that? Is there anything about Roy Palmer that you can tell us?

Well, Roy Palmer, he was playing with, when I first got him, he was playing with Amos Raleigh. You know who I talk about Amos Raleigh? Yes. A corn-ed player. Well, he used to be with that, I believe if I'm mistaken, it was the Tulane Band. The Tulane Band. That was Amos Raleigh. He was a corn-ed player. Well, Amos, this fellow used to play with him. And, uh, this other fellow, what's the name again? He used to play tram on wood, him. And then he started going, he went to wood too. Well, I found it out and I don't know if he's dead or what.
No, he's still living. I saw him last year.

Yeah, where's he? In Chicago. Still in Chicago. I'll tell you why. Because I got a, I got a postal card from, uh, from, uh, George Christmas, you know? And, uh, and, but he's not here. John Foster? Yeah, Pops Foster, they call it sometimes. Yeah, Pops Foster. I got a, I got a card from him Christmas. Every year, he is, I don't know if I, how you do it, but he send a Christmas card to me and tell me that, Mr. and Mrs. Foster. Christmas call to me and tell me that Mr. and Mrs. Foster.

I said, well I didn't know you was married. I sent a part back to him and I told him, well Mr. and Mrs. I didn't know you ever got married, George. Well, George is kind of, he like to joke funny foolishness and all that, you know? But of course he's a good bass player. I must say, he's a good bass player. Now I don't know if Johnny Lentz is living yet.
No, no, he's dead. He's dead too. In Chicago last year they told me Herbert Lindsay was living, but I couldn't find him.

That's what I heard. Yeah. Some people knew him, did you ever know a Mary Mack? You remember a vaudeville team, Mack and Mack? Yeah. Mary Mack. Yeah. She came from across the river. Fess knew her. Yeah. Minetta. And they're up in Chicago and they said they saw a Herbert Lindsay within the last, it'll be two years now. He could be dead by this time. Yeah. But I couldn't, they couldn't find him when I was there and I didn't, never did see him.
And I don't know if he's in Chicago or where. Well I left, I left them in Chicago and I came back home. I left them all over. The whole bank stayed up there.
The whole bank stayed up there.
